Paint each mailbox a color so that mailboxes that sit next to one another on the curb are not painted the same color and limit the palette to the smallest possible size.
Choose a spotlight gel color for every musician position so that adjacent performance areas are lit with different gels and minimize the variety of gels used.
Select a background color for each road sign so that signs visible from the same approach never use the same background and keep the number of background colors as low as possible.
Assign a stripe color to every aquarium tank so that tanks sharing filtration connections do not have the same stripe and minimize the number of stripe colors.
Place an endcap label color on each bookshelf so that shelves that touch side by side do not share the same label color and use as few label colors as possible.
Assign paint colors to all rooms so that any rooms that share a wall are painted in different colors, and use as few distinct paints as possible.
Pick wireless channel labels for each access point so that points with overlapping coverage use different labels, and minimize the total number of channel labels used.
Label every bookcase section with a tag color so that adjoining sections have different tag colors, using the smallest possible variety of tag colors.
Decide façade paint colors for all buildings on the block so that buildings that touch do not have the same color, and keep the number of paint colors as low as possible.
Assign colored signs to garden beds so that neighboring beds display different sign colors, minimizing how many sign colors are needed.
Select backdrop colors for each photo booth so that booths that stand side by side have different backdrop colors, and use as few backdrop tones as possible.
Assign accent colors to exhibit rooms so that adjacent rooms are accented differently, and keep the palette size as small as possible.
Allocate frequency band names to wireless microphones so that microphones whose ranges interfere are assigned different bands, and minimize the number of distinct bands in use.
Pick tile glaze colors for a mosaic so that tiles that touch are glazed differently, minimizing the number of glaze colors required.
Assign jersey colors to all teams so that teams scheduled to play one another do not wear the same jersey color, and use the fewest jersey colors overall.
Choose placemat colors for dining tables so that neighboring tables have different placemat colors, while keeping the variety of placemat colors minimal.
Select highlight colors for menu items so that adjacent items use different highlights, and minimize how many highlight colors appear across the menu.
Assign ribbon colors to centerpieces so that centerpieces positioned next to each other have different ribbon colors, using as few ribbon colors as possible.
Choose carpet swatch colors for office zones so that adjoining zones are covered with different swatches, and minimize the number of swatch colors used.
Assign costume accent colors to characters so that any pair of characters who appear together wear different accents, and minimize the total number of accent colors.
Pick signage color schemes for gates so that gates that are next to each other use different schemes, while minimizing how many schemes are needed.
Choose awning colors for shops so that shops that share a wall have different awning colors, and keep the number of awning colors as small as possible.

global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of students in the robotics club (the number of vertices). Every listed student should receive exactly one badge color.

global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of student collaborations or project pairings (the number of edges). Each collaboration links two students who must not share the same badge color.

item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a collaboration: the identifier (index or name) of the first student in a collaborating pair. This student must have a different badge color than the paired student.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of handheld radios (devices) in the cul-de-sac that each need a channel assigned — corresponds to the graph's vertex count.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unordered pairs of radios that can interfere with each other and therefore must be assigned different channels — corresponds to the graph's edge count.

global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of conference rooms in the building; equals the number of vertices in the graph and the number of swatches that must be assigned (one per room).

item_fields.name: v

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of employees in the shop who will each be assigned exactly one uniform color; corresponds to the number of vertices in the graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one employee in an adjacent pair; this employee stands next to the employee identified by 'v' and therefore must wear a different uniform color from them.

item_fields.name: v

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second mannequin in the adjacency pair (a label or index referencing one of the total_mannequins). Together with 'u' denotes an unordered pair of neighboring mannequins that must wear different colors.

global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct regions (areas) on the hand‑drawn map that must each be assigned exactly one marker hue.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacent region pairs (undirected touching relationships along boundaries) — each corresponds to a constraint that the two touching regions must receive different hues.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one region in a specific touching pair; together with the matching 'v' identifier it denotes two regions that share a boundary and therefore must have different hues.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other region in the touching pair; paired with 'u' to specify the adjacency (boundary) between these two regions that prohibits the same hue for both.

global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of radio masts (base stations) in the grid that each must be assigned exactly one frequency; corresponds to the total vertex count in the graph.

global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of unordered pairs of masts whose coverage areas overlap (i.e., edges in the graph). Each such pair represents two masts that must not be assigned the same frequency.

global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of product categories on the shelf — i.e., the count of distinct items (vertices) that must each be assigned a color label.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency relationships between categories — i.e., how many unordered pairs of categories sit next to each other and therefore must receive different labels.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier (index or name) for one category in an adjacent pair — one endpoint of an adjacency; this category must have a different label than the paired category.

item_fields.name: v

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the other chair in the touching pair (an integer ID referring to a specific chair). This represents the other endpoint of an adjacency; the two endpoints (chair_id_u and chair_id_v) must receive different seat-cover patterns.

global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct volunteers who will receive a single badge color each; corresponds to the number of vertices in the graph.

global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of unordered volunteer pairs who work together on a shift (each pair is one edge); each such pair must have different badge colors.

item_fields.name: u

item_fields.name: v

item_fields.name: v

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the second lane in an adjacency (the other endpoint of an edge). Paired with 'lane_a_id', it specifies a touching lane pair that must use distinct colors.

item_fields.name: v

item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or ID) of one endpoint module in a direct dependency pair. Together with the paired module it forms an unordered dependency edge — both modules must be colored and must not share the same channel color.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or ID) of the other endpoint module in the dependency pair. It pairs with the corresponding module_a to denote a direct dependency that forbids the same release channel color for both.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of mailboxes in the neighborhood map — each mailbox requires exactly one paint color in the coordinated scheme.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of pairs of mailboxes that sit next to each other on the curb; each such pair represents a constraint that those two boxes must be painted different colors.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one mailbox in an adjacent pair (one endpoint of the curb adjacency); used together with 'mailbox_two_id' to indicate two side-by-side boxes that cannot share the same paint.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other mailbox in the adjacent pair (the other endpoint); together with 'mailbox_one_id' it denotes a pair of neighboring mailboxes that must be painted different colors.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of musician marks (distinct spotlight positions) on stage that each need exactly one gel color assigned.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of adjacency relationships between positions — each counts a pair of neighboring performance areas that must be lit with different gels.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one end of an adjacent pair: the first musician position in a neighboring relationship (an integer label for a mark).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other end of an adjacent pair: the neighboring musician position that must use a different gel than position_a.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of road signs in the arrangement — i.e., the number of vertices to assign background colors to.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of pairs of signs that are visible together from at least one approach (each such pair is an edge and must not share the same background).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of one sign in a pair that are visible simultaneously from some approach — this vertex cannot share a background with the paired sign.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of the other sign in the visible pair — this vertex cannot share a background with sign_a_id.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of aquarium tanks that need a stripe assigned; every tank must receive exactly one stripe color and this count is the number of vertices in the filtration-connection graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct filtration links between tanks; each link connects two tanks and is an undirected connection that requires those two tanks to have different stripe colors.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of one tank at one end of a filtration connection; this tank must have a different stripe from the tank identified by the corresponding 'v' field.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the other tank at the other end of the same filtration connection; together with 'u' it denotes a pair of tanks that share a filtration link and therefore cannot share the same stripe.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of bookshelves that will receive an endcap label — i.e., the number of vertices in the shelf adjacency graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unordered pairs of shelves that touch side-by-side; each such pair is an adjacency that requires those two shelves to have different endcap label colors (i.e., the number of edges).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One shelf in an adjacent pair (identified by its shelf index or label). Together with 'shelf_b' this denotes two shelves that meet side-by-side and therefore must not share the same endcap label color.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other shelf in an adjacent pair (identified by its shelf index or label). Paired with 'shelf_a' to indicate a side-by-side contact requiring different endcap label colors.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of rooms in the layout that must be painted. This is the count of vertices in the graph and tells you how many room labels/assignments are required.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairs of rooms that share a wall. This equals the number of adjacency constraints (edges) and indicates how many room-to-room painting conflicts must be avoided.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one of the two rooms that share a wall. This room must be painted a different color from the room referenced by the corresponding 'v' field.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other room in the shared-wall pair. Together with the 'u' field it defines an undirected adjacency: these two rooms touch and therefore cannot use the same paint.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of wireless access points (hotspots) that must be assigned a single channel label. This is the count of vertices in the overlap graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unordered hotspot pairs whose coverage areas overlap. Each such pair is a constraint forbidding the two listed hotspots from using the same channel.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or name) of the first hotspot in an overlapping pair. Together with 'v', it specifies two hotspots whose coverage overlaps and therefore must use different channel labels.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or name) of the second hotspot in an overlapping pair. Paired with 'u', it marks a constraint that these two hotspots cannot share the same channel.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of shelf cubby sections that need a colored tag; each cubby is a vertex in the graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of pairs of cubbies that touch along an edge or corner and therefore must use different tag colors; each such pair is an edge in the graph.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one cubby in an adjacent pair (uses the same indexing as total_cubbies, e.g. integers). Together with 'v' it denotes two touching cubbies that must have different tag colors.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other cubby in the touching pair corresponding to 'u'; together they form an adjacency that forbids the same tag color on both cubbies.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of buildings on the block that need a single façade color; corresponds to the number of vertices in the graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unordered pairs of buildings that touch each other (adjacent façades); corresponds to the number of edges in the graph and each such pair must be painted different colors.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (e.g., index, address, or label) for the first building in a touching pair; together with building_b_id it denotes two buildings whose façades touch and therefore must not share the same paint color.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second building in the touching pair corresponding to the same edge; paired with building_a_id to indicate the two neighboring buildings that must have different façade colors.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of raised garden beds that need one colored sign each; this is the number of vertices in the layout.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairs of beds that touch along an edge or corner and therefore must display different sign colors; this equals the number of edges in the layout.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) for the first bed in a neighboring pair; used to indicate one endpoint of a touching relationship that forbids the same sign color on both beds.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) for the second bed in a neighboring pair; paired with 'bed_a_id' to denote two beds that touch and therefore must have different sign colors.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of photo booths in the lineup — i.e., the number of vertices in the graph and the number of backdrops that must be assigned (one per booth).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unordered pairs of booths that stand side by side — i.e., the number of adjacency constraints (edges). Each such pair must have different backdrop tones.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) for one booth in a side-by-side pair. Together with 'v' it specifies an adjacency: these two booths share a side and therefore must not have the same backdrop color.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) for the other booth in a side-by-side pair. Paired with 'u', it marks an adjacency constraint that forbids assigning the same backdrop tone to both booths.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of exhibit rooms that need an accent color; corresponds to the number of vertices in the layout graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency pairs (room-to-room connections where accents must differ); corresponds to the number of undirected edges in the layout graph.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of one endpoint room in a specific adjacency; this room is adjacent to room_b and therefore must be assigned an accent different from that room.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the other endpoint room in the same adjacency; room_b is adjacent to room_a and must have a different accent color. Adjacencies are undirected, so order between room_a and room_b does not matter.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of wireless microphones to label (the number of vertices in the interference graph). Each microphone must be assigned exactly one frequency band name.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of unordered pairs of microphones whose coverage ranges overlap (the number of edges). Each listed pair cannot share the same band name.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Integer identifier of one microphone in an overlapping pair; this microphone must be assigned a different band than the microphone named by 'v'.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Integer identifier of the other microphone in an overlapping pair; this microphone must be assigned a different band than the microphone named by 'u'.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of tiles in the mosaic — the count of distinct pieces (vertices) that each must receive exactly one glaze color.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of touching tile pairs in the mosaic — each represents a pair of tiles that share an edge (are adjacent) and therefore must be glazed in different colors.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the first tile in a touching pair — one endpoint of an adjacency that must not share the same glaze as its paired tile.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second tile in a touching pair — the other endpoint of the adjacency; this tile must have a different glaze than tile_a_id.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of teams in the tournament — the number of vertices that must each be assigned a single jersey color. Team IDs run across this set (e.g., 1..total_teams).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of scheduled matches (pairings) between teams — the number of edges. Each match is a constraint: the two teams involved cannot wear the same jersey color.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one team in a scheduled match (one endpoint of an edge). This team must be assigned a single jersey color different from the other team in the same match entry.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other team in a scheduled match (the other endpoint of the edge). The jersey color assigned to this team must differ from the team_a_id in the same match.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of dining tables in the hall — i.e., the number of vertices. This is how many placemats must be assigned (one per table).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of neighboring-table relationships — i.e., the number of edges. Each represents a pair of tables that touch or are close enough to be considered adjacent and therefore must have different placemat colors.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the first table in a neighboring pair. Together with 'v' this denotes an undirected adjacency: table_u_id must not share the same placemat color as table_v_id.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second table in a neighboring pair. Together with 'u' this denotes an undirected adjacency: table_v_id must not share the same placemat color as table_u_id.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of menu entries that need a highlight color — i.e., the number of vertices in the menu adjacency graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of adjacency relationships between menu entries — each represents a pair of neighboring items that must use different highlight colors.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of the first menu entry in an adjacent pair; used together with 'v' to indicate two neighboring entries that cannot share the same highlight.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of the second menu entry in an adjacent pair; paired with 'u' to mark two adjacent entries that must receive different highlight colors.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of centerpieces that need ribbons (i.e., the number of vertices in the graph). Use this to know how many distinct centerpiece labels there are to color.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of unordered touching pairs of centerpieces (i.e., the number of edges). Each pair represents two centerpieces placed next to each other that must not share the same ribbon color.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of one centerpiece in a touching pair; this is one endpoint of an adjacency and must receive a different ribbon than its partner.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of the other centerpiece in the touching pair; together with 'centerpiece_a' this describes two adjacent centerpieces that cannot share the same ribbon color.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of office zones that need a carpet swatch assigned — i.e., the number of vertices in the adjacency graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairs of zones that touch each other and therefore must receive different carpet swatches — i.e., the number of edges in the graph.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) for one of the two adjoining office zones in a touching pair; this zone must have a different swatch than the paired zone.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) for the other office zone in the adjoining pair; together with zone_one_id this denotes a border between two zones that cannot share the same swatch.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of characters in the cast who each must be assigned exactly one costume accent color (i.e., the number of vertices in the appearance graph).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct character pairings that appear together and therefore cannot share the same accent color (i.e., the number of edges in the appearance graph).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One character in a specific pairing — an endpoint of an appearance pair. This is an identifier for the first character involved in a mutual-appearance constraint; order is not meaningful.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other character in that pairing — the second endpoint of the mutual-appearance constraint. This identifier, paired with character_a, denotes two characters who must have different accent colors.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of gates that need a signage color scheme (this equals the number of vertices). Every gate must receive exactly one scheme.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of neighboring gate pairs (this equals the number of undirected edges). Each pair marks two gates that sit next to each other and therefore cannot share the same color scheme.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the first gate in an adjacent pair (one endpoint of an edge). Use this ID when specifying which two neighboring gates must have different schemes.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the second gate in an adjacent pair (the other endpoint of an edge). Together with gate_one_id it defines a pair of neighboring gates that require different schemes.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of storefronts that need awnings (the number of vertices in the graph). This counts every shop that must be assigned exactly one awning color.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairs of shops that share a wall (the number of edges). Each such pair represents a constraint: those two shops cannot use the same awning color.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one shop in a specific adjacency pair (one endpoint of an edge). Together with 'shop_b' it denotes two shops that share a wall and therefore must have different awning colors.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other shop in the adjacency pair (the other endpoint of an edge). Paired with 'shop_a' to indicate a wall-sharing relationship that forbids them from using the same awning color.
